# 0. Purpose and project layout

This document continues from Task 1. It (a) re-runs the preprocessing reproducibly with **relative paths**, (b) closes the gaps found when the Task 1 checks were extended (illogical values, missing values, linkage), and (c) builds the three final tables used by the Shiny app, one per task abstraction.

```
project/
  02_task2A_processing.Rmd     <- this file
  data/raw/                    <- ORIGINAL files exactly as supplied (nothing edited by hand)
  data/processed/              <- created by this file; read by the Shiny app
```

Put the 7 CSVs, `LGA_2021_LGA_2024.csv`, `32350DS0003_2024.xlsx` and both `.geojson` files in `data/raw/`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr); library(readxl); library(dplyr); library(tidyr)
library(stringr); library(sf); library(knitr)

raw_dir <- "data/raw"
out_dir <- "data/processed"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# 1. Import and structural checks

**Step.** Before importing, the number of fields on every line of each CSV is counted. A line with a different count from the header signals a structural problem such as an unintended comma inside a number. A file that imports without an error is not automatically correct.

```{r structure}
field_check <- function(f) {
  n <- count.fields(file.path(raw_dir, f), sep = ",", quote = "\"", comment.char = "")
  tibble(file = f,
         data_rows = length(n) - 1,
         header_fields = n[1],
         lines_off_spec = sum(n != n[1]),
         first_bad_line = if (any(n != n[1])) which(n != n[1])[1] else NA_integer_)
}
csvs <- c("LGA_2021_LGA_2024.csv", "lga_area.csv", "lga_details.csv", "lga_adjacents.csv",
          "lga_sector.csv", "lga_stops_routes.csv", "routes_city_freq.csv")
structure_check <- bind_rows(lapply(csvs, field_check))
kable(structure_check, caption = "Field-count check on the raw CSV files")
```

Two files have one off-spec line each: `lga_area.csv` (Yarra Ranges, `1,611.9332`) and `lga_sector.csv` (Cardinia, `1,283`). Both are thousands separators that split one number into two fields.

**Treatment.** The raw files are left untouched. The fix is applied in code (so it is reproducible and the manual step is documented), and the number of lines changed is checked to be exactly one per file.

```{r repair}
fix_thousands <- function(file, col_types) {
  lines <- read_lines(file.path(raw_dir, file))
  pat <- ",(\\d{1,3}),(\\d{3})(\\.\\d+)?(?=,|$)"
  hit <- str_detect(lines, pat)
  lines <- str_replace(lines, pat, ",\\1\\2\\3")
  tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv"); write_lines(lines, tf)
  list(data = read_csv(tf, col_types = col_types, show_col_types = FALSE),
       lines_fixed = sum(hit), which = which(hit))
}

a <- fix_thousands("lga_area.csv",
  cols(lga_code21 = "c", lga_name21 = "c", sqkm = "d", cbd_euclidean_km = "d"))
s <- fix_thousands("lga_sector.csv",
  cols(lga_code21 = "c", lga_name21 = "c", sector = "c", lga_sqkm = "d", lga_part_sqkm_pct = "d"))

lga_area   <- a$data
lga_sector <- s$data
stopifnot(a$lines_fixed == 1, s$lines_fixed == 1,
          ncol(lga_area) == 4, nrow(lga_area) == 36,
          ncol(lga_sector) == 5, nrow(lga_sector) == 41)

kable(tibble(file = c("lga_area.csv", "lga_sector.csv"),
             lines_fixed = c(a$lines_fixed, s$lines_fixed),
             rows_after = c(nrow(lga_area), nrow(lga_sector)),
             cols_after = c(ncol(lga_area), ncol(lga_sector))),
      caption = "After repair: expected 4 and 5 columns")
```

```{r import-rest}
blank_to_na <- function(df) df %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), "")))

mapping <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "LGA_2021_LGA_2024.csv"),
                    col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
lga_details <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "lga_details.csv"),
                        col_types = cols(lga_code21 = "c", lga_name21 = "c", .default = "d"))
lga_adjacents <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "lga_adjacents.csv"),
                          col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>% blank_to_na()
stops_routes_raw <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "lga_stops_routes.csv"),
                             col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>% blank_to_na()
route_freq <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "routes_city_freq.csv"),
                       col_types = cols(vehicle = "c", route_number = "c", route_name = "c",
                                        daily_freq = "d", weekday_freq = "d", weekend_freq = "d")) %>%
  blank_to_na()

lga_area_geo <- st_read(file.path(raw_dir, "lga_area.geojson"), quiet = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(lga_code21 = as.character(lga_code21))
stops_geo <- st_read(file.path(raw_dir, "stops.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
```

Empty strings (`""`) were converted to `NA` so that "missing" is counted consistently. This is why Task 1 reported 2,959 missing values in the stop-route file (2,953 `route_number` + 6 `route_name`).

# 2. ABS population (Table 3)

**Issue found in Task 1.** The sheet was read with `skip = 5`, which makes the age-group row the header and leaves a units row (`no.`) as the first data row. The result was 23 character columns, so no number could be used. Table 3 also contains a national total row and footnotes.

**Treatment.** Read without a header, set explicit names, keep only rows that have a numeric state code (this removes the units row, the national total and the footnotes), then convert to numeric.

```{r population}
pop_raw <- read_excel(file.path(raw_dir, "32350DS0003_2024.xlsx"),
                      sheet = "Table 3", col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text")

age_cols <- c("age_0_4","age_5_9","age_10_14","age_15_19","age_20_24","age_25_29",
              "age_30_34","age_35_39","age_40_44","age_45_49","age_50_54","age_55_59",
              "age_60_64","age_65_69","age_70_74","age_75_79","age_80_84","age_85_plus")

aus_total <- as.numeric(pop_raw[[23]][which(pop_raw[[4]] %in% "Total Persons Australia")])

pop <- pop_raw %>%
  setNames(c("st_code", "st_name", "lga_code24", "lga_name24", age_cols, "total_persons")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(st_code, "^[0-9]+$")) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(c(age_cols, "total_persons")), as.numeric))

pop_checks <- tibble(
  check = c("LGA rows kept", "Missing values", "Duplicate LGA codes",
            "Rows where age groups do not sum to Total persons",
            "Sum of LGAs minus the ABS national total row"),
  result = c(nrow(pop), sum(is.na(pop)), sum(duplicated(pop$lga_code24)),
             sum(rowSums(pop[age_cols]) != pop$total_persons),
             sum(pop$total_persons) - aus_total))
kable(pop_checks, caption = "ABS Table 3 validation (expect 547 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0)")

pop_vic <- pop %>% filter(st_name == "Victoria") %>% select(lga_code24, lga_name24, population = total_persons)
kable(tibble(scope = c("Australia (all LGAs)", "Victoria"),
             lgas = c(nrow(pop), nrow(pop_vic)),
             population = c(sum(pop$total_persons), sum(pop_vic$population))),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Population before and after filtering to Victoria")
```

# 3. LGA versions: linking 2021 codes to 2024 population

The transport and boundary files use ASGS **2021** codes and the population uses **2024** codes. Joining directly by code is tested first to show what would go wrong, then the crosswalk is used.

```{r crosswalk}
naive <- lga_area %>% left_join(pop_vic, by = c("lga_code21" = "lga_code24"))
cat("Direct join on code: LGAs with no population =", sum(is.na(naive$population)), "->",
    paste(naive$lga_name21[is.na(naive$population)], collapse = ", "), "\n")

lga_ref <- lga_area %>%
  left_join(mapping, by = c("lga_code21" = "LGA_CODE_2021")) %>%
  left_join(pop_vic, by = c("LGA_CODE_2024" = "lga_code24"))

kable(lga_ref %>% filter(lga_code21 != LGA_CODE_2024) %>%
        select(lga_name21, lga_code21, LGA_NAME_2024, LGA_CODE_2024, population),
      caption = "LGAs whose code or name changed between 2021 and 2024")

stopifnot(!anyNA(lga_ref$LGA_CODE_2024), !anyNA(lga_ref$population), nrow(lga_ref) == nrow(lga_area))
```

A direct join silently loses **Moreland** (2021 code 25250), which became **Merri-bek** (2024 code 24700). The crosswalk matches all 36 LGAs and no rows are lost or duplicated. Joining by name would also fail for this LGA, which is why codes plus the mapping table are used.

# 4. Scope: which records belong in the analysis

```{r scope}
scope_tbl <- tibble(
  file = c("lga_stops_routes.csv", "lga_stops_routes.csv", "lga_stops_routes.csv", "lga_sector.csv"),
  step = c("Rows as supplied (all Victoria)",
           "Rows in the 36 assessment LGAs",
           "After removing exact duplicate rows",
           "LGAs in the 36-LGA list but missing from this file"),
  value = c(nrow(stops_routes_raw),
            sum(stops_routes_raw$lga_code21 %in% lga_area$lga_code21),
            nrow(distinct(filter(stops_routes_raw, lga_code21 %in% lga_area$lga_code21))),
            length(setdiff(lga_area$lga_code21, lga_sector$lga_code21))))
kable(scope_tbl, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

stops_routes <- stops_routes_raw %>%
  filter(lga_code21 %in% lga_area$lga_code21) %>%
  distinct()
```

* The stop-route file covers **80** Victorian LGAs, but the assessment list (`lga_area.csv`) has **36**. The other 44 regional LGAs (9,460 rows, e.g. Greater Geelong, Ballarat) are out of scope and removed.
* **4 exact duplicate rows** (all Moonee Valley, stops 19270 and 19276) are removed. They are repeats of the same stop-route pair, not different services.
* Remaining repeated `stop_id` values are legitimate: one stop serves several routes. Each indicator therefore states whether it counts records, unique stops or unique routes.

## Decision: Unincorporated Vic

```{r uv}
uv <- lga_ref %>% filter(lga_name21 == "Unincorporated Vic") %>%
  transmute(lga_name21, sqkm, population,
            stop_route_records = sum(stops_routes$lga_code21 == lga_code21),
            unique_routes = n_distinct(stops_routes$route_name[stops_routes$lga_code21 == lga_code21]))
kable(uv, caption = "Unincorporated Vic profile")
```

It is a valid geographic record but has 0.18 km², 964 residents and 2 stop records. Per-km² and per-resident ratios would be driven by tiny denominators and would not be comparable with normal LGAs. **Decision: excluded from all indicators, maps and rankings (35 LGAs analysed), but kept in the raw-data tab and documented.**

```{r study}
study_lga <- lga_ref %>% filter(lga_name21 != "Unincorporated Vic")
stopifnot(nrow(study_lga) == 35)
sr <- stops_routes %>% filter(lga_code21 %in% study_lga$lga_code21)
```

# 5. Further quality checks (illogical values, missing values, linkage)

## 5.1 Frequency file (`routes_city_freq.csv`)

```{r freq-checks}
route_freq <- route_freq %>%
  mutate(route_key = paste(vehicle, coalesce(route_number, ""), coalesce(route_name, ""), sep = "|"))

freq_checks <- tibble(
  check = c("Routes (rows)",
            "Missing route_number (legitimate, e.g. V/Line coaches)",
            "Routes where daily_freq is outside weekday/weekend range (+-1)",
            "daily_freq <= 0",
            "Duplicate vehicle + route_number (non-missing)",
            "Duplicate vehicle + route_number + route_name"),
  result = c(nrow(route_freq),
             sum(is.na(route_freq$route_number)),
             sum(route_freq$daily_freq < pmin(route_freq$weekday_freq, route_freq$weekend_freq) - 1 |
                 route_freq$daily_freq > pmax(route_freq$weekday_freq, route_freq$weekend_freq) + 1),
             sum(route_freq$daily_freq <= 0),
             sum(duplicated(route_freq[!is.na(route_freq$route_number), c("vehicle", "route_number")])),
             sum(duplicated(route_freq$route_key))))
kable(freq_checks)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(route_freq$route_key))
```

* Frequencies are plausible (all positive; `daily_freq` lies between the weekday and weekend values).
* **Missing `route_number` is not an error** (the metadata says so), so rows are kept.
* `vehicle + route_number` is **not unique** (5 pairs repeat, e.g. bus 675, 843, 900 and the Pakenham train line, because each direction or variant has its own name). Joining on it would duplicate rows and inflate frequencies. The **three-part key `vehicle | route_number | route_name`** is unique (0 duplicates) and is used everywhere. Missing parts become an empty string so the key is always defined.

## 5.2 Linking stop-route records to frequencies

```{r link}
sr <- sr %>% mutate(route_key = paste(vehicle, coalesce(route_number, ""), coalesce(route_name, ""), sep = "|"))

keys_all <- stops_routes %>%
  mutate(route_key = paste(vehicle, coalesce(route_number, ""), coalesce(route_name, ""), sep = "|")) %>%
  distinct(vehicle, route_number, route_name, route_key)

unmatched <- keys_all %>% anti_join(route_freq, by = "route_key")
kable(tibble(
  measure = c("Distinct routes in the 36 LGAs", "...with a frequency record", "...without a frequency record",
              "Routes in frequency file not found in stop-route file"),
  value = c(nrow(keys_all), nrow(keys_all) - nrow(unmatched), nrow(unmatched),
            nrow(anti_join(route_freq, keys_all, by = "route_key")))),
  caption = "Route linkage (expect 498 / 453 / 45 / 0)")
kable(head(unmatched %>% select(vehicle, route_number, route_name), 12),
      caption = "Examples of routes with no frequency record")
```

**Why it matters.** 45 routes (mostly regional coaches and local bus routes such as 941, 951, 959, 978-982) have no frequency record. The file is a "city" frequency file, so they are simply absent.

**Treatment (assumption stated).** Missing frequency is **never set to zero**. Unmatched routes are still counted in route counts, but are left out of frequency totals and averages. The share of an LGA's routes that have a frequency (`freq_match_rate`) is carried into the final tables and shown in the app, because LGAs with low match rates have understated frequency totals.

## 5.3 Contextual tables (not used in the three indicators, but checked)

```{r context-checks}
adj_missing <- lga_adjacents %>% filter(is.na(lga_code21))
kable(adj_missing, caption = "lga_adjacents.csv: rows with a missing primary LGA code")

lga_adjacents <- lga_adjacents %>%
  left_join(lga_area %>% select(lga_name21, code_from_area = lga_code21), by = "lga_name21") %>%
  mutate(lga_code21 = coalesce(lga_code21, code_from_area)) %>% select(-code_from_area)
stopifnot(!anyNA(lga_adjacents$lga_code21))

kable(lga_details %>% filter(if_any(education:public, is.na)), caption = "lga_details.csv: missing counts")
kable(lga_details %>% arrange(desc(higher_education)) %>% head(3), caption = "Highest higher_education counts")
lga_details <- lga_details %>% mutate(higher_education = if_else(higher_education > 50, NA_real_, higher_education))

sector_check <- lga_sector %>% group_by(lga_code21, lga_name21) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(lga_part_sqkm_pct), parts = n(), .groups = "drop")
kable(tibble(check = c("Range of lga_part_sqkm_pct", "LGAs whose shares do not sum to 1", "LGAs split across sectors"),
             result = c(paste(range(lga_sector$lga_part_sqkm_pct), collapse = " to "),
                        sum(abs(sector_check$total - 1) > 0.01), sum(sector_check$parts > 1))))
```

* **Wyndham** has a missing code in 3 adjacency rows. It is recovered from `lga_area.csv` by exact name (one Wyndham, code 27260), not guessed.
* **Melbourne** has all four facility counts missing (kept as `NA`, not zero). **Darebin** has `higher_education = 100`, over 12 times the next highest value (8), so it is treated as suspicious and set to `NA`. The true value cannot be recovered. These facility counts are context only and are not used in the indicators.
* `lga_part_sqkm_pct` is a **proportion from 0 to 1**, not a percentage despite its name. Shares sum to 1 for every LGA. Five LGAs span two sectors.
* `stops.geojson` has 28,977 points but only 28,546 distinct `stop_id` values and 353 missing `mb_code_2021`. All 21,385 stop IDs used in the CSV are present. Indicators are counted from the CSV; the point file is only used for optional map points, after de-duplicating by `stop_id`.

# 6. Task abstraction 1 (raw values): scale of service

**Action-target.** *Explore* the spatial distribution of public transport service **volume** (unique stops, unique routes, total daily frequency) across Greater Melbourne LGAs.

**Tables and variables.** `lga_stops_routes` (`lga_code21`, `stop_id`, `vehicle`, `route_number`, `route_name`), `routes_city_freq` (`daily_freq`), `lga_area.geojson` (geometry).

| Indicator | Rule |
|---|---|
| Stop-route records | `n()` rows per LGA (shown for transparency only) |
| **Unique stops** | `n_distinct(stop_id)` per LGA |
| **Unique routes** | number of distinct `route_key` per LGA |
| **Total daily frequency** | `sum(daily_freq)` over **distinct LGA-route pairs** that have a frequency record |

Frequency is summed only after removing repeated LGA-route pairs. Otherwise a route with 40 stops in an LGA would be counted 40 times. A route that crosses several LGAs contributes its full route-level `daily_freq` to each LGA it serves (assumption: frequency is a route property, not LGA-specific).

```{r ta1}
stop_counts <- sr %>%
  group_by(lga_code21) %>%
  summarise(stop_route_records = n(),
            unique_stops = n_distinct(stop_id),
            vehicle_types = n_distinct(vehicle),
            vehicle_mix = paste(sort(unique(vehicle)), collapse = " + "),
            .groups = "drop")

lga_route <- sr %>%
  distinct(lga_code21, route_key) %>%
  left_join(route_freq %>% select(route_key, daily_freq), by = "route_key")

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(lga_route[c("lga_code21", "route_key")]))

route_counts <- lga_route %>%
  group_by(lga_code21) %>%
  summarise(unique_routes = n(),
            routes_with_freq = sum(!is.na(daily_freq)),
            total_daily_freq = sum(daily_freq, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_daily_freq = mean(daily_freq, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(freq_match_rate = routes_with_freq / unique_routes)

ta1 <- study_lga %>%
  select(lga_code21, lga_name21) %>%
  left_join(stop_counts, by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(route_counts, by = "lga_code21") %>%
  select(lga_code21, lga_name21, stop_route_records, unique_stops, unique_routes,
         total_daily_freq, routes_with_freq, freq_match_rate)

stopifnot(nrow(ta1) == 35, !anyDuplicated(ta1$lga_code21), !anyNA(ta1$unique_stops),
          all(ta1$unique_stops <= ta1$stop_route_records))
kable(ta1 %>% arrange(desc(unique_stops)) %>% head(8), digits = 2, caption = "TA1 final table (top 8 by unique stops)")
```

# 7. Task abstraction 2 (processed values): service intensity

**Action-target.** *Compare* service intensity across LGAs using derived indicators (density and average frequency), grouped by dominant metropolitan sector.

**Tables and variables.** TA1 table + `lga_area` (`sqkm`) + `lga_sector` (`sector`, `lga_part_sqkm_pct`).

| Indicator | Formula |
|---|---|
| **Stops per km²** | `unique_stops / sqkm` |
| Routes per km² | `unique_routes / sqkm` |
| **Average daily frequency** | `mean(daily_freq)` over the LGA's distinct routes **that have a frequency record** (average per route, not per stop) |
| **Dominant sector** | sector with the largest `lga_part_sqkm_pct`. A tie goes to the more central sector (Inner, then Middle, then Outer). |
| Sector mix label | text such as "Inner 50% / Middle 50%", for display only |

The dominant sector describes **area overlap only**. Service values are never split by sector share.

```{r ta2}
sector_levels <- c("Inner Melbourne", "Middle Melbourne", "Outer Melbourne")

dominant <- lga_sector %>%
  mutate(sector_order = match(sector, sector_levels)) %>%
  arrange(lga_code21, desc(lga_part_sqkm_pct), sector_order) %>%
  group_by(lga_code21) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(lga_code21, dominant_sector = sector)

sector_mix <- lga_sector %>%
  mutate(sector_order = match(sector, sector_levels)) %>%
  arrange(lga_code21, sector_order) %>%
  group_by(lga_code21) %>%
  summarise(sector_mix = paste0(str_remove(sector, " Melbourne"), " ",
                                round(lga_part_sqkm_pct * 100), "%", collapse = " / "),
            .groups = "drop")

ta2 <- ta1 %>%
  left_join(study_lga %>% select(lga_code21, sqkm, cbd_euclidean_km), by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(route_counts %>% select(lga_code21, avg_daily_freq), by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(stop_counts %>% select(lga_code21, vehicle_types, vehicle_mix), by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(dominant, by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(sector_mix, by = "lga_code21") %>%
  mutate(stops_per_km2 = unique_stops / sqkm,
         routes_per_km2 = unique_routes / sqkm,
         dominant_sector = factor(dominant_sector, levels = sector_levels)) %>%
  select(lga_code21, lga_name21, sqkm, cbd_euclidean_km, unique_stops, unique_routes,
         stops_per_km2, routes_per_km2, avg_daily_freq, vehicle_types, vehicle_mix,
         dominant_sector, sector_mix, freq_match_rate)

stopifnot(nrow(ta2) == 35, !anyNA(ta2$dominant_sector), !anyNA(ta2$stops_per_km2),
          all(is.finite(ta2$avg_daily_freq)))
kable(ta2 %>% count(dominant_sector), caption = "LGAs per dominant sector")
kable(ta2 %>% arrange(desc(stops_per_km2)) %>% select(lga_name21, stops_per_km2, avg_daily_freq, dominant_sector) %>% head(8),
      digits = 2, caption = "TA2 final table (top 8 by stop density)")
```

# 8. Task abstraction 3 (normalised / indexed): fair comparison by population

**Action-target.** *Rank* LGAs by a composite **Transport Service Availability Index (0-100)** built from population-normalised indicators.

**Tables and variables.** TA1 table + population (ABS 2024 Table 3 via the 2021 to 2024 crosswalk).

| Step | Formula |
|---|---|
| Per-capita indicators | `stops_per_1000 = unique_stops / population * 1000`, `routes_per_1000 = unique_routes / population * 1000`, `freq_per_1000 = total_daily_freq / population * 1000` |
| Min-max scaling (0-100) | `x' = (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x)) * 100`, computed across the 35 LGAs |
| **Index** | **Equal weights** of 1/3 each: `index = (stops' + routes' + freq') / 3` |
| Rank | 1 = highest index (ties share the lower rank number) |

**Why equal weights.** No evidence in the data says one dimension (coverage, route variety or frequency) matters more, so equal weights are the most transparent default. All three components are "higher = more service", so no direction reversal is needed. The index is **relative** (0 = lowest of these 35 LGAs, 100 = highest), not an absolute standard of good service.

```{r ta3}
minmax100 <- function(x) (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x)) * 100
w <- c(stops = 1/3, routes = 1/3, freq = 1/3)
stopifnot(abs(sum(w) - 1) < 1e-9)

ta3 <- ta1 %>%
  left_join(study_lga %>% select(lga_code21, LGA_CODE_2024, LGA_NAME_2024, population), by = "lga_code21") %>%
  mutate(stops_per_1000  = unique_stops / population * 1000,
         routes_per_1000 = unique_routes / population * 1000,
         freq_per_1000   = total_daily_freq / population * 1000,
         stops_scaled    = minmax100(stops_per_1000),
         routes_scaled   = minmax100(routes_per_1000),
         freq_scaled     = minmax100(freq_per_1000),
         service_index   = w[["stops"]] * stops_scaled + w[["routes"]] * routes_scaled + w[["freq"]] * freq_scaled,
         index_rank      = rank(-service_index, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  arrange(index_rank)

stopifnot(nrow(ta3) == 35, !anyNA(ta3$population), !anyNA(ta3$service_index),
          all(ta3$service_index >= 0 & ta3$service_index <= 100),
          min(ta3$stops_scaled) == 0, max(ta3$stops_scaled) == 100)

kable(ta3 %>% select(index_rank, lga_name21, population, stops_per_1000, routes_per_1000,
                     freq_per_1000, service_index, freq_match_rate),
      digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "TA3 final table (full ranking)")

cat("Population of the 35 analysed LGAs:", format(sum(ta3$population), big.mark = ","),
    "| 36 LGAs incl. Unincorporated Vic:", format(sum(study_lga$population) + uv$population, big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

# 9. Save analysis-ready outputs for the Shiny app

```{r save}
lga_indicators <- ta1 %>%
  left_join(ta2 %>% select(lga_code21, sqkm, cbd_euclidean_km, stops_per_km2, routes_per_km2,
                           avg_daily_freq, vehicle_types, vehicle_mix, dominant_sector, sector_mix),
            by = "lga_code21") %>%
  left_join(ta3 %>% select(lga_code21, population, stops_per_1000, routes_per_1000, freq_per_1000,
                           stops_scaled, routes_scaled, freq_scaled, service_index, index_rank),
            by = "lga_code21")

stopifnot(nrow(lga_indicators) == 35, !anyDuplicated(lga_indicators$lga_code21))

lga_map <- lga_area_geo %>%
  filter(lga_code21 %in% lga_indicators$lga_code21) %>%
  select(lga_code21) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  left_join(lga_indicators, by = "lga_code21")
stopifnot(nrow(lga_map) == 35, !anyNA(lga_map$unique_stops))

saveRDS(ta1, file.path(out_dir, "ta1_raw_values.rds"))
saveRDS(ta2, file.path(out_dir, "ta2_processed_values.rds"))
saveRDS(ta3, file.path(out_dir, "ta3_normalised_index.rds"))
saveRDS(lga_indicators, file.path(out_dir, "lga_indicators.rds"))
saveRDS(lga_map, file.path(out_dir, "lga_map.rds"))
write_csv(lga_indicators, file.path(out_dir, "lga_indicators.csv"))
```

# 11. Refinements since Task 1

In response to feedback, the Task 1 plan was made reproducible without changing the three analytical ideas: formal action-target wording, explicit formulas, a unique LGA-route key, route frequency counted once per LGA-route pair, a defined dominant-sector rule, treatment of unmatched routes, and explicit min-max scaling with equal weights. Population is expressed per **1,000** residents, as in the original plan.
